headline: Every can checked, even at two million a day.
label: #F4F1E8
heroLede: Asahi Beverages' $60 million can line at Yatala, which it calls Australia's biggest brewery, can fill more than two million cans every 24 hours of beers like Great Northern, VB and Carlton Dry. At that speed, nobody can read every label and date by eye. This is what a camera check could look like on a can line like yours. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every can has its end on and seated, with no visible damage around the seam. It looks at what can be seen from outside, so it adds to your seam checks rather than replacing them.
labelLede: Full strength and mid strength cans can look almost the same at line speed, and the wrong one in a carton is a complaint and a possible withdrawal. The camera checks every can carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: At two million cans a day, a date coder that slips for ten minutes is a lot of stock. The system reads the printed best-before and batch code on every can and compares them with the beer and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Can ends, label backing and carton offcuts can all end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four ends not seated in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the seamer.
